Comments:
- The loader does make calls into the Windows Driver interface to find drivers, so the loader very well could have a bug in it preventing accurate results from these interfaces. `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices` returning 0 is worrying, as that Availability of 'Running/Full Power' likely means 'this is the device to use'.
- Can you try setting the environement variable `VK_LOADER_DEBUG=all` and posting the log that gets output? The log should go to stdout, so you can redirect that as necessary. That log should at least tell us what the loader thinks it's seeing and if it's seeing anything wrong that would cause it do deliberately drop ICDs (which sometimes happens when there's errors).
- I suppose there's no other way to set the env var at the right time and redirect stdout than with a .bat file? That makes it quite unhandy. I'll add it as an option for players to start through that in our beta build, but it might take a long time to get results. If there was a debug callback with the info, it would be a lot cleaner to integrate to give to end-users.
- The `VK_EXT_debug_utils` extension will report the exact same information. If it's easier for you to use that method and dump it to a log file, that'll work just as well. That method typically takes a bit longer to set up (though I don't know your use case) but it's definitely a better solution in the long term.
- Actually, I should add one more comment to my last post. The debug utils extension will get all of the messages that loader generates _once the extension is enabled_. The extension is not enabled until instance creation time, which I believe means that it'll miss all messages related to finding and loading drivers. It will still log what's going on in `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices`, but there's a chance that the problem is actually happening earlier, in which case the environment variable will be necessary to get the log messages. If it's easier for you to just log the messages from debug utils, that should help, though it may turn out that we need to use the envar.
- I've set up both, albeit launch with envar has to be manually selected by the user. I'll report back when I get some hits. If there was a way to set the envar and redirect the stdout in code after the process has started, I could automate that as well and get more hits. Vulkan Loader seems to check the envar when the library is loaded (I assume that's on process start because we link with the dll?), since setting the envar in code before interacting with Vulkan doesn't seem to achieve anything. Also was not able to find a way to redirect stdout except with a batch file on Windows, which is a huge bummer.
- I wonder if this issue has something to do with VK_LAYER_NV_optimus, VK_LAYER_AMD_switchable_graphics or an interaction between the two layers. All those machines have both installed.
- Maybe there is an interaction between those two layers resulting in zero physical devices getting through. The VK_LAYER_NV_optimus works based on what the user chooses from the NVIDIA control panel. On a laptop under the "Manage 3D settings" section of the control panel there will be a "Global Settings" option called "Preferred graphics processor". With the VK_LAYER_NV_optimus implicit layer it works like this: - "Auto-select": No changes to the physical devices and its up to the Vulkan application to choose. - "High-performance NVIDIA processor": Non-NVIDIA GPUs are filtered out, leaving only NVIDIA physical devices. - "Integrated graphics": NVIDIA GPUs are filtered out, leaving only non-NVIDIA physical devices. I can imagine if the user has "High-performance NVIDIA processor" selected and there is something similar on the AMD side that filters out non-AMD physical devices, then you'll end up with nothing. To help diagnose this issue, these implicit layers can each be disabled with the following environment settings: ``` set DISABLE_LAYER_AMD_SWITCHABLE_GRAPHICS_1=1 set DISABLE_LAYER_NV_OPTIMUS_1=1 ```
- @username_3 What's the downside of disabling the two layers?
- I don't know about the AMD layer, but filtering is all that the NVIDIA layer does. The downside would be that the NVIDIA control panel preferred graphics processor setting, and the more advanced per-application preferred graphics processor settings, would no longer work, and Vulkan applications that don't explicitly select the appropriate physical device might end up running the application on an unexpected physical device. This could end up being a bad user experience if, for example, their browser ends up running on the dGPU or their game ends up running on the iGPU. Disabling the layers globally should only be done for debugging the issue.
- I don't know if the layers are loaded in the order that they are reported by `vkEnumerateInstanceLayerProperties`, but if that's the case, it would fit your explanation: ˙VK_LAYER_NV_optimus` is listed first and `VK_LAYER_AMD_switchable_graphics` second.
- @username_0, have you tried either generating a log from the loader's output or disabling the layers as @username_3 suggested? It's not clear from what you posted if you attempted those actions and without knowing the outcome of at least one of those actions it's pretty hard to diagnose.
- Unfortunately I don't have access to these machines, but I will hopefully have more information a couple weeks.
- Ok, then I'll leave the issue as is for the time being. Post here whenever you have more info.
- I got another report of a new laptop with AMD iGPU and NVIDIA dGPU having an issue with Vulkan. I was able to remote into the machine to see what was going on. In its default state, simply running "vulkaninfo" failed with the following: ```vkEnumeratePhysicalDeviceGroupsKHR failed with ERROR_INITIALIZATION_FAILED``` Setting ```set DISABLE_LAYER_AMD_SWITCHABLE_GRAPHICS_1=1``` fixed the problem. Setting ```set DISABLE_LAYER_NV_OPTIMUS_1=1``` made no difference - it still failed. Another work around was to use the NVIDIA control panel and select either "High-performance NVIDIA processor" or "Integrated graphics" from Manage 3D settings->Preferred graphics processor. Either of these options causes there to be only one physical device enumerated. This indicates to me there is a bug with the VK_LAYER_AMD_switchable_graphics layer with its vkEnumeratePhysicalDeviceGroupsKHR function when there is more than one physical device enumerated. I installed the very latest Adrenalin 21.2.3 driver, but the bug was still there.
- Looks like the issue I'm seeing is this one: https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/AMDVLK/issues/196
- AMD is looking into this issue now and will get back to this thread soon.
- AMD confirmed this issue is exactly same as the [AMDVLK#196](https://github.com/GPUOpen-Drivers/AMDVLK/issues/196) and the fix is on the way to be released. So far only apps calling **vkEnumeratePhysicalDeviceGroupsKHR** will be impacted.
- Glad things are getting fixed, but it sounds like a different issue since we are not calling `vkEnumeratePhysicalDeviceGroupsKHR`.
- @username_0 I assume you hit this issue when you run vulkaninfo? vulkaninfo will call `vkEnumeratePhysicalDeviceGroupsKHR`.
- We're not running vulkaninfo. We're running a custom vulkan game engine that powers Warhammer 40,000: Gladius and some players are having the issue I described in the initial issue description. We've since deployed a build with ``` DISABLE_LAYER_AMD_SWITCHABLE_GRAPHICS_1=1 DISABLE_LAYER_NV_OPTIMUS_1=1 ``` and the issue is entirely gone. Unfortunately I don't have any new logs that would help. Our beta test build didn't get any hits on the error and resolving the issue was higher priority than getting `VK_LOADER_DEBUG=all` logs.
- I have a system with the following specs: AMD Ryzen 7 4800H APU, RTX 2060, running Nvidia Game Ready Driver v466.11 I get the following while running vulkaninfo: `WARNING: [Loader Message] Code 0 : ReadDataFilesInRegistry: Registry lookup failed to get layer manifest files. The selected gpu (0) is not a valid GPU index. The available GPUs are in the range of 0 to 4294967295.` Vulkan also doesn't show up as supported in GPU-Z for both AMU iGPU and NVIDIA dGPU.
- With the latest release from AMD, driver:AMD_Graphic_DriverOnly_ROG_AMD_B_V27.20.14044.2001_23051 We still see no vulkan capable device enumeration, either with the nvidia dedicated GPU, or with the AMD iGPU. This is on an Asus TUF A15. Last I read in the Nvidia support forums, they throw the ball to AMD.
- The fix is in the reference/generic AMD driver that Asus have not begun using yet.
- Thanks, will wait for it. Meanwhile, we advised users to setup the env variables.
- The Vulkan loader recently was updated with a warning if a layer modified the number of GPUs exposed via the `vkEnumeratePhysicalDevices` entry-point. Since any more will require more advanced loader logging, I'm going to close this issue and track the updated logging separately.
- I also encountered this problem with my lenovo Laptop. I wanted to get some information from the vulkaninfoSDK.exe that comes with the SDK, but it was just not running at all. Only the vkcube.exe showed the error, which is how i found this issues. Changing the GPU in windows settings did nothing for me, only the environment variable solutions resolved the issue. I used it on the vulkaninfoSDK.exe and switched between the two environment variables. I found that when disabling Optimus both GPUs showed up, the same as when disabling both. So it seems like optimus is selecting the GPU to use for the application, but the AMD equivalent is just giving me all GPUs. The problems with the AMD layer might not be solved on some systems and versions, so using the environment variable solution might be the best option for me. But it is not very elegant, so I wanted to ask if there is a better solution to achieve the same, but without a ugly bat file.
- @username_9 You can set the env vars in code before initializing Vulkan.
- Thanks, im gonna try that.

Title:
[CosmosDB] Query fails when setting partition_key

Description:
- **Package Name**: azure-cosmos - **Package Version**: 4.1.0 - **Operating System**: Ubuntu 18.04 LTS - **Python Version**: 3.8 **Describe the bug** I created a test CosmosDB database using the Azure web portal with the examples from the [CosmosDB Getting Started](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/sql-query-getting-started) documentation. ```json { "id": "AndersenFamily", "children": ["..."], "..." }, { "id": "WakefieldFamily", "children": ["..."], "..." }, ``` I set the `partition_key` on the container to be the `"id"` field. I can run the following queries (from the [SQL Query Object Array](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/sql-query-object-array) page) via the "Data Explorer" on the Azure web portal just fine, but the Python SDK has issues when I set `partition_key` on the query. The following two queries work fine in Data Explorer on the Azure web portal: ```sql SELECT * FROM Families.children SELECT * FROM c IN Families.children ```` Both queries throw errors in the Python SDK when I pass a `partition_key` parameter to `query_items()`: ```python import os from azure.cosmos.cosmos_client import CosmosClient client = CosmosClient(os.environ['COSMOS_ENDPOINT'], credential=os.environ['COSMOS_KEY']) container = client.get_database_client('testdb').get_container_client('testcontainer') query1 = 'SELECT * FROM Families.children' query2 = 'SELECT * FROM c IN Families.children' # these work just fine list(container.query_items(query=query1, enable_cross_partition_query=True)) list(container.query_items(query=query2, enable_cross_partition_query=True)) # both of these throw the same error list(container.query_items(query=query1, partition_key='AndersenFamily')) list(container.query_items(query=query2, partition_key='AndersenFamily')) ``` ``` CosmosHttpResponseError: (BadRequest) Message: {"errors":[ {"severity":"Error","location":{"start":4294967295,"end":4294967295},"code":"SC2001","message":"Identifier 'Families' could not be resolved."}]} ActivityId: 5e53c5f6-43bc-43ee-90a7-4e39d48aa271, [...] ``` **Expected behavior** Setting `partition_key` on `query_items()` should not cause an error. **Additional context** I suspect that this may be related to the bug reported in #11721. However, my example here is much simpler and identifies the issue with passing a `partition_key` argument to `query_items()`.

Comments:
- @username_2 Can you look into this? May be an issue with the samples for how to do query
- Hello @username_0 Tks for the feedback. We will check it out. As a workaround you can use 'select children from Families'. BTW, you sample code has 'testcontainer' instead of Families, but I think that it's a copy/paste error. Tks for the contribution!
- Hello @username_0 I'm closing this issue because it's a documentation problem, what I will start to address today. Basically what is happening is that your are narrowing down the scope with the FROM clause: instead of Families, and all of it's properties, your "dataset" only has the children property. And the partition key isn't there. Tks for the help to improve the product.
- @username_2 Thanks for looking into this issue. However, I'm not convinced that narrowing down the scope in the `FROM` clause is the problem. As explained in the [official CosmosDB SQL syntax for the FROM clause](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cosmos-db/sql-query-from), `FROM Families.children` is certainly valid syntax. It is a `<container_expression> '.' property_name`. Plus, the queries work just fine in Data Explorer on the Azure web portal. This is clearly an issue with the Python SDK, not with my query.

I have an asynchronous UISearchBar setup as follows: Inherit UISearchDisplayDelegate & set it up for myController.SearchDisplayController.Delegate Override ShouldReloadForSearchString -> start a new thread calling a web service and return false to not reload the UITableView Web service completes in background -> call BeginInvokeOnMainThread() Reload tableview via myController.SearchDisplayController.SearchResultsTableView.ReloadData() Everything works on the first search I make, I can backspace or type and see new results pop in asynchronously. Every background thread seems to be calling BeginInvokeOnMainThread() properly as well. Is this most likely a bug in MonoTouch? If this is likely, I can create a repro. Answers:
- This is not a binding bug (I checked them to be sure). The data source should be set on the UISearchDisplayController , not on the table view (e.g. SearchDisplayController.SearchResultsTableView ). IOW replace: SearchDisplayController.SearchResultsTableView.Source = _tableSource; with: SearchDisplayController.SearchResultsSource = _tableSource; This will ensure the internal state of UISearchDisplayController is updated properly between uses.

Am I doing something wrong ? From my experience. Without paths GOGM can processed queries that return just a node. Something like this: ``` MATCH (n)-[..]-(..) WHERE ... RETURN n ``` But when you need relations and nodes, you need to use paths. From my code, such query doesn't work (same with `RETURN *`): ``` MATCH (object{twinId:"..."})-[r:IS_DESCRIBED_BY]->(value:ReferenceInformationObject{twinId:".."}) WHERE value.name in [...] RETURN object,r,value ``` But paths GOGM process correctly: ``` MATCH p=(object{twinId:"..."})-[r:IS_DESCRIBED_BY]->(value:ReferenceInformationObject{twinId:"..."}) WHERE value.name in [...] RETURN p ``` In my code, I always use paths for GOGM queries.
